Crl.M.A. 13912/2023(Exemption)

1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application is disposed of.

1. This petition has been filed for quashing of FIR No. 103/2019 registered at Janakpuri, New Delhi under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC on the ground that the parties have settled their disputes vide MOU dated 12th January, 2023 which is on record of this Court.
Petitioner No. 1 and respondent No. 2 (complainant) are present through VC and are duly identified by their counsels and the IO.
Petitioners Nos. 2-4 are also present in Court and are duly identified by their counsels and the IO.
2. Petitioner No. 1 and respondent No. 2 were married on 25th This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 21:48:11 November, 2016 and have lived together in United States of America but due to disputes and differences the marriage ended in divorce vide decree dated 25th April, 2023 which is also on record of this Court.
No child was born out of wedlock.

3. As per settlement balance amount of Rs. 24,66,000/- is being tendered by DD No. 592348 drawn on Bank Punjab National Bank dated 20th May, 2023 along with the jewellery articles and is being received by the Power of Attorney holder respondent No.2 Ms. Taranbir Kaur (the mother of respondent No.2).

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Respondent No.2 states that she has no objection to the said FIR considering that all aspects of the settlement have been complied with and she has duly authorised her mother to receive the said draft and jewellery articles on her behalf.

Ms. Taranbir Kaur (the mother of respondent No.2)
acknowledges the receipt of the same.

5. Considering the above settlement between the parties and the chances of conviction of the petitioners being remote and bleak, there is no use continuing with proceedings of the present FIR as it would be a misuse of the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.
Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, the FIR No. 103/209 under Sections 498A/406/34 IPC registered at PS Janakpuri, New Delhi and proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
6. Parties shall abide by the terms of settlement.
7. Accordingly, the petition is disposed of.
Pending applications (if any) are disposed of as infructuous.
8. Copy of the order be given dasti under the signature of the Court Master.
ANISH DAYAL, J MAY 22, 2023/RK
